label: input n at original positions 3-6
explanation: Fires whenever the input token is the letter n during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at positions 3 through 6. On those steps it is active essentially 100% of the time, and on dev it is active nowhere else. It stays silent for n at positions 0-2 (apart from tiny ~0.04 activations at t=2), for n at positions 7-8, for n echoed back in the copy phase (a handful of ~0.05 traces), and for every other token. Magnitude per activation is highest at positions 4-5, lower at 3, and lowest at 6. A repeated n (not its first occurrence) tends to activate more weakly, and so does a context with many digits. Neighbouring tokens, first token, and L have little effect beyond that.

issues: Test split: precision 1.0, recall 0.9996, F1 0.9998, mass recall 0.99997. The reported 'recall 1, F1 1' is rounded. The 20 missed test steps hold 0.0% of activation mass: ~0.04 traces for n at t=2 and ~0.03-0.07 traces where n is echoed in the copy phase (copying an original n from position 0). This is scattered, negligible noise, not a systematic class.

No false positives on test. The by-orig_idx profile shows a rate of 0.033 (about 1/30 of the vocab) at each of positions 3-6, so the feature fires on essentially every n at those positions. It fires zero times at positions 0, 1, 7 and 8, and at every other token.
The magnitude claim checks out: mass per activation is about 1.64e-5 at t=3, 2.66e-5 at t=4, 2.46e-5 at t=5 and 1.16e-5 at t=6, so it peaks at 4-5, is lower at 3 and lowest at 6.
Not separately verified: the minor claims that repeated n and digit-heavy contexts activate more weakly (score does not give per-condition magnitude). They do not affect the label or predicate.
